quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: As your blood alcohol content (BAC) increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content (BAC) measures the amount of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest thing to do?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive slower than other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when some drivers go much faster or slower than the traffic around them. Drive at the same speed as other vehicles, as long as you stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When can you drive through a stop sign intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering an intersection with a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering. Then proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the side of the road and empty.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop as long as the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is out.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while talking to them while driving.
Only watches the car in front of them.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, searching for items, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming while driving. Always scan the road, check your mirrors, and watch your dashboard regularly. These habits keep you attentive.

questions.question: Which of these can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sleeping pills.
Cough syrup and cold medicine with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs impair your driving. These include sleeping pills and tranquilizers, over-the-counter cough syrup and cold medicine (which may contain alcohol or antihistamines), and illegal drugs.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test your vehicle's suspension.
They vibrate and make noise to warn drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They vibrate and make noise to warn drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create vibrations and noise to alert drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and may run in front of your vehicle without looking.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights (if you have them) when driving in fog. High beams point upward and bounce off fog back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed ahead and pull in front of the cyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a cyclist, slow down and give them plenty of space. Cyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: Before driving, you must remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all your vehicle's windows and mirrors. Remove all snow, ice, and frost before driving.

questions.question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels and causes loss of steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels and causes loss of steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels. This causes you to lose steering control. Drive slowly on icy roads to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lanes you want to enter or cross. Be ready to stop if other traffic is coming, but you can keep going if the way is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: Signs for public recreation areas are:

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs point to historic sites and recreation areas. They help you find places to visit.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Usually affect only large vehicles.
Only reduce visibility.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can blow dust and dirt onto the road and can physically move your vehicle.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you can proceed in that direction when the road is clear. This is true even if the main light is red.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle uses its siren and flashing lights, you must yield by:

options.text: Moving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping immediately, even in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: When you see and hear an emergency vehicle, drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after it passes.

questions.question: If you are driving too slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down even more.
Pull over to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if you are driving so slowly that cars are backed up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Wave your arms.
Turn on your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, honk your horn to alert them.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians who are crossing against the traffic light.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Be aware that pedestrians may cross against the light by mistake.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is correct?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.
As you drive faster, you should increase the distance between your car and the car ahead.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is unlikely. Faster speeds require longer stopping distances, so you need to leave more space between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells you the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.
